title: A headless worker's session hooks leave no query log distill process in its worktree that makes land refuse it
goal: SP-5x5ut5ko retrospective: the first two headless workers each left five or six querylog.py distill --settle processes running in their worktree (distills of other sessions' transcripts waiting up to USAGE_LOCK_WAIT_S, 600 s, for the distill lock); land refused both branches at step branch until they exited (about 9 minutes), and it recurred at SP-qg7ncs6d, SP-m3azo2y7 and SP-tm4wlsve. A worker's session-end hook starts its distill with the working directory and script in the clone's main checkout, so land finds no process of it in the worktree and no longer stops at step branch; and land's refusal for a process that still runs there says a distill waits up to USAGE_LOCK_WAIT_S for the lock and to run land again, not 'end it'.

gates.question: Where does a worker's session-end distill run so land finds no process of it in the worker's worktree?
options: outside: querylog launch starts the distill with its working directory and script in the clone's main checkout, never the linked worktree
wait: land keeps waiting for such a distill up to USAGE_LOCK_WAIT_S plus its run before it refuses
remove: land removes the worktree past a distill whose output is distill.log and says so
gates.recommendation: outside: querylog launch starts the distill with its working directory and script in the clone's main checkout, never the linked worktree
gates.answer: outside: querylog launch starts the distill with its working directory and script in the clone's main checkout, never the linked worktree

notes: Premise: ql_distill.detach starts a session-end distill with cwd=str(HOME), the checkout the running copy of the tools is in, so a worker's distill has its worktree as working directory (planned 2026-10-12: run detach from a worktree and read its cwd with lsof: it was the worktree root). Merged BG-5qbzoc7n (bl_land.py:932 says 'end it' after the 60 s wait though a distill waits up to 600 s on the usage lock) and ST-a755ciys (SP-etslk6yu: the 60 s wait, 8e655b04f, is shorter than a distill on the lock). Recurrences: SP-qg7ncs6d (ST-yztru4mz, pid 73924 ran 3 min after the worker exited), SP-m3azo2y7 (BG-6cq4zeai, about 6 min behind three distills), SP-tm4wlsve (ST-2rg6tn6r, stopped after 60 s, hook ran 8 min). The suite sits at max_ids 100: extend a test and rename it to carry the name each check selects, no new id. Gate distill-where answered: outside. Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 15 of 19, "Land snags: session-end distill, a stopped land's worktree, an orchestrator behind main and a racy hook test"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates. SP-4o3plg4l close, 2026-10-12: land of BG-pedsqeqs stopped at step branch for about 10 minutes: a session-end querylog.py distill (ppid 1) sat in the worker's worktree waiting up to USAGE_LOCK_WAIT_S=600 for the distill lock another distill held. SP-lmf4ke4w close, 2026-10-12: recurred twice: land of ST-2nvlf6jo and ST-zrysu6ri stopped at step branch (land.end exit=1, 60 s each) behind the three workers' session-end distills of another session's transcript (45fdbca2), waiting on the distill lock a main-checkout distill (pid 27202) held; they cleared after about 7 minutes.
